tasks.short: Join student recruitment, registration and placement

steps.what: Read the student recruitment calendar in the {CALENDAR}.
Read the entry rules in the {DOCS} for recruitment activities.
Draft an unsaved sheet of those recruitment activities.
Check the recruitment sheet against the calendar and the entry rule.
File only the accepted recruitment sheet in the {DOCS}.
Participate in student recruitment activities and explain the programme.
Join the registration meeting and say which session still needs a place.
Advise on placement for a student and leave the decision in the room.

tasks.design: She reads the student recruitment calendar in the {CALENDAR} and the entry rules in the {DOCS}. A deterministic sheet copies session, time, place and that entry rule and does not save. She checks those fields. A separate step files only the accepted sheet in the {DOCS}. She still takes part in the activities, still speaks at the registration meeting, and still advises on placement in the room. Nothing is sent outside.
tasks.previous_blocker: The session list lived in the calendar and the entry rule lived in a separate document, so the sheet was copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: The calendar already holds session, time and place, and the entry rule is already written, so a sheet can copy those fields for her to accept or reject.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a student fits a programme is a conversation, and the register is not hers to close.
tasks.human_edge: She is in the room with the prospective student and can hear the question.
tasks.altitude: She still spends the open day in the room. She no longer copies the sheet, but she still accepts it before it is filed, and she still does not place a student.

reach.task: state the entry rule at a recruitment activity
reach.learn: which entry rule must be on the sheet before the activity

evidence.claim: She still explains the programme, still speaks at the registration meeting, and still advises on placement in the room. The only shorter work is writing and filing the sheet from the calendar and the entry rule she read. Model knowledge.
Annex III point 3 covers admission, evaluating learning outcomes, setting the education level, and detecting cheating in tests.
Emotion inference in education has been banned since February 2025.

assumptions: The {CALENDAR} already stores session, time and place. She reads those fields in s1. The entry rule is a written rule she reads in s2. The sheet only copies those fields. If a field is missing she types it. The sheet does not invent it.
The sheet names no student. It does not admit, place, grade, or set an education level. Filing it in the {DOCS} is inside the institution. A wording change voids the filing.

The open-day talk, the registration meeting and the placement advice are not shortened. Speaking in the room is not a send outside the organisation. An outbound mail or a public advert would be its own gated step and is not built.
The 8 already-counted hours are the check in s4 and are not subtracted again. The 4 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a sheet.
No step infers a student's emotion.
unknowns: Whether today's calendar stores session, time and place as separate fields.
How often she currently writes the sheet, rather than keeping the sessions in her head.
research_questions: What share of recruitment sheets she rejects because a session changed after she read the calendar.

already_counted.description: Checking the sheet against the calendar and the entry rule is already in s4.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected recruitment sheet herself, beyond the check already in s4.

approvals.approved_version: Recruitment sheet she accepted in s4: session, time and place from the calendar she read, plus the entry rule she read, with no named student and no admission or placement. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a day she keeps the plan in her head and rewrites the sheet, only filing a sheet she already accepted is shorter, about 3. On a day the calendar is stable she accepts the draft, so both the writing and the filing are shorter, about 9. The 4 hours of rewrite upkeep are already taken off the central 16.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the charter of the student organizations in the {DOCS}.
Draft an unsaved note of the charter limits for those organizations.
Check each limit and accept that exact note for the advisers.
File only the accepted note for those student organizations in the {DOCS}.
Advise the student organizations in the room on the event they asked about.
Coordinate with colleagues in the room when an organization still needs a room.

tasks.design: She reads the charter in the {DOCS}. A deterministic note copies the written limits and does not save and does not write advice. She checks each limit. A separate step files only the accepted note in the {DOCS}. She still advises the student organizations in the room and still asks a colleague in the room for a space. Nothing is sent outside.
tasks.previous_blocker: The charter limits were in a document, and she retyped them before each meeting with an organization.
tasks.enabler_now: The charter already states the limits, so a note can copy them for her to accept or reject.
tasks.still_hard: What an organization should do about its event is advice she gives in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She knows the students in the organization and can hear what they are asking.
tasks.altitude: She still spends the meeting with the organization. She no longer copies the charter, but she still accepts the note before it is filed, and the advice stays hers.

reach.task: sit with a student organization while the adviser is present
reach.learn: which charter limit the note may repeat and which advice it must not add

evidence.claim: Advising the student organizations stays with her in the room. The only shorter work is copying the charter limits and filing the note she accepted. Model knowledge.
Annex III point 3 covers admission, evaluating learning outcomes, setting the education level, and detecting cheating in tests.
Emotion inference in education has been banned since February 2025.

assumptions: The charter in the {DOCS} already states the limits. She reads them in s1. The note only copies those limits. If a limit is missing she types it. The note does not add advice.
The note is not an admission, a grade, or a level. Filing it in the {DOCS} is inside the institution. A wording change voids the filing.
The advice in the room and the talk with a colleague are not shortened. Neither is a send outside the organisation.
The 8 already-counted hours are the check in s3 and are not subtracted again. The 3 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a note.
No step infers a student's emotion, and the note does not monitor staff.
unknowns: Whether the charter is stored as separate limits she can copy, or only as continuous prose.
How often a charter changes during a term.
research_questions: What share of charter notes she rejects because a limit was amended after she read it.

already_counted.description: Checking each charter limit against the charter she read is already in s3.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected charter note herself, beyond the check already in s3.

approvals.approved_version: Charter note she accepted in s3: each limit copied from the charter she read, with no advice added. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a term the charter changed and she rewrites the note, only filing a note she already accepted is shorter, about 3. On a term the charter is stable she accepts the draft, so both the writing and the filing are shorter, about 10. The 3 hours of rewrite upkeep are already taken off the central 16.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise teaching, internship and research work

steps.what: Read the undergraduate or graduate research brief in the {DOCS}.
Draft an unsaved agenda of the agreed research or internship points.
Check the agenda against the research brief and accept it.
File only the accepted research agenda in the {DOCS}.
Supervise the teaching, internship or research work in the meeting.
Decide in the room whether the undergraduate work may continue.

tasks.design: She reads the research brief in the {DOCS}. A deterministic agenda copies title, next step and deadline and does not save. She checks it against the brief. A separate step files only the accepted agenda in the {DOCS}. She still supervises the teaching, internship or research work in the meeting and still decides in the room whether the work may continue. The agenda is not a result and is not sent out.
tasks.previous_blocker: The brief held the title and the next step, and she rewrote the agenda before each supervision meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: The brief already states title, next step and deadline, so an agenda can copy those fields for her to accept or reject.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the work may continue is a judgement in the meeting, and she does not set the result.
tasks.human_edge: She has read the work and can question the student in the meeting.
tasks.altitude: She still spends the supervision meeting with the student. She no longer copies the agenda, but she still accepts it before it is filed, and the continue decision stays in the room.

reach.learn: which next step was already in the brief and must not be treated as a result

evidence.claim: The supervision meeting and the continue-or-stop judgement stay with her. The only shorter work is copying the agenda from the brief and filing the agenda she accepted. Model knowledge.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set the result under article 7.12c.
Emotion inference in education has been banned since February 2025.

assumptions: The brief in the {DOCS} already states title, next step and deadline. She reads those fields in s1. The agenda only copies them. If a field is missing she types it. The agenda does not judge the work.
The agenda is not a result under article 7.12c and is not sent to the examination board. The spoken continue decision is not filed and is not a grade. A wording change voids the filing.
The supervision meeting and the continue decision are not shortened. Speaking in the meeting is not a send outside the organisation. A letter to an internship host is not built.
The 10 already-counted hours are the check in s3 and are not subtracted again. The 4 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects an agenda.
The brief can name a student, so access to it needs a check. No step infers a student's emotion.
unknowns: Whether the brief already stores title, next step and deadline as separate fields.
Which examination board appoints the examiner for this programme.
research_questions: What share of agendas she rejects because the brief changed after she read it.

already_counted.description: Checking the agenda against the research brief is already in s3.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected research agenda herself, beyond the check already in s3.

approvals.approved_version: Research agenda she accepted in s3: title, next step and deadline copied from the brief she read, with no result and no continue decision. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When she rejects the agenda and writes it herself, only filing an agenda she already accepted is shorter, about 3. When the brief is stable she accepts the draft, so both the writing and the filing are shorter, about 9. The 4 hours of rewrite upkeep are already taken off the central 16.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the government or industry question in the {EMAIL}.
Write the professional consulting points she will provide.
Draft an unsaved consulting note for that government or industry client.

loop.input: Only the consulting points she wrote in s2, after she read the question.
loop.output: An unsaved consulting note. Nothing is stored and nothing is sent.
loop.check: Every recommendation and every figure in the note appears in her points. A new conclusion, or a number she did not write, is rejected.
loop.stop: One pass. If the check fails she writes the note herself and nothing is sent.
loop.why_not_simpler: Copying the points does not turn them into a note a ministry or a firm can read.

steps.what: Check each recommendation and figure, then accept the consulting note.
Send the accepted consulting note by {EMAIL} to that government or industry client.
Meet the client and explain the consulting services she will stand behind.

tasks.design: She reads the question in the {EMAIL} and writes the consulting points herself. Those points are not filed. A bounded loop drafts an unsaved note from those points only, and the check rejects any recommendation or figure she did not write. She accepts that exact note. A separate step sends only that accepted note from the {EMAIL}. She still meets the client and explains the services. The meeting is not the send.
tasks.previous_blocker: The client question arrived by mail, and she wrote the note by hand before she would send it.
tasks.enabler_now: She already writes the points, so a draft can turn only those points into a note she accepts or rejects before anything is sent.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a recommendation is one she will stand behind is her judgement, and the meeting with the client stays hers.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which figure is unpublished and which conclusion she did not write.
tasks.altitude: She still meets the client. She accepts the note before a separate step sends it, and she does not hand over the consulting judgement.

reach.task: answer a government or industry question in their field
reach.learn: which conclusion must match points they wrote before a note is sent

evidence.claim: The client meeting stays with her. The only shorter work is drafting the note from points she wrote and sending the note she accepted. Model knowledge.
A note to a government or industry client can carry unpublished figures. She sends it only after she has accepted the wording, and confidential client material is not uploaded. Model knowledge.

assumptions: She writes the consulting points in s2. They are the only input to the draft. They are not filed and not sent. If the draft check fails she writes the note herself.
The send in s5 is the only step that leaves the organisation. It sends the exact note she accepted in s4. A wording change voids it. The meeting in s6 is a talk, not a send.
Confidential client material is not uploaded. The draft does not add a figure or a conclusion she did not write.
The 12 already-counted hours are the check in s4 and are not subtracted again. The 5 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a note.
National rules on professional advice vary. This design does not file a formal opinion with a public register.
unknowns: Whether this client expects the note by mail, or only the meeting.
Which figures in the question are unpublished.
research_questions: What share of drafts she rejects because a figure or a conclusion was not in her points.

already_counted.description: Checking each recommendation and figure against the points she wrote is already in s4.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected consulting note herself, beyond the check already in s4.

approvals.approved_version: Consulting note she accepted in s4: only recommendations and figures that appear in the points she wrote, with no new conclusion. A wording change voids it. The send uses this version and no other.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When she rejects the draft and writes the note herself, only the send of a note she already accepted is shorter, about 4. When she accepts the draft, both the writing and the send are shorter, about 12. The 5 hours of rewrite upkeep are already taken off the central 20.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Her week stays on teaching, open days, advising, supervision and the client meeting. She accepts the recruitment sheet, the organisation note, the supervision agenda and the consulting note before each is filed or sent. She does not hand over placement, the organisation advice, the research judgement, or the consulting judgement.
skills_to_grow: Checking a recruitment sheet against the calendar and the entry rule she read.
Checking a charter note against the written limits, with no advice added.
Checking a research agenda against the brief, and not treating it as a result.
Checking a consulting note against points she wrote before it is sent.
role.ambitious_version: She still takes part in recruitment, still advises student organizations, still supervises the work, and still meets the client. The only changes are a recruitment sheet filed from the calendar and the entry rule she checked, a charter note filed from limits she checked, a research agenda filed from the brief she checked, and a consulting note sent only in the wording she accepted.
